payload.title: Stream Sockets
payload.summary: Build bounded POSIX stream-socket loops with explicit framing, partial-I/O handling, and monotonic deadlines.

prerequisites: C17 arrays, pointers, explicit lengths, and fixed-width integers
File descriptors, byte order, and the POSIX socket lifecycle
outcomes: Explain why TCP is a byte stream rather than a message transport
Complete sends and exact receives despite partial system calls
Recover application boundaries with length-prefixed frames
Distinguish EOF, truncation, timeout, capacity, malformed input, and system errors

events.label: Start 1000 ms deadline
events.detail: The loopback exchange uses one absolute monotonic deadline for accept, receive, echo send, and client receive.

events.label: Connect to loopback :0
events.detail: The client connects to the kernel-selected 127.0.0.1 port after listen has established the local server.

events.label: Write length prefix fragment
events.detail: The first fragment is three bytes, 00 00 00, so the receiver cannot decode the six-byte payload length yet.

events.label: Write boundary-crossing fragment
events.detail: The second fragment is 06 73 74, completing the length prefix and starting payload bytes st.

events.label: Write payload fragment
events.detail: The third fragment is 72 65 61, continuing the payload as rea without creating an application message boundary.

events.label: Write final payload byte
events.detail: The final one-byte fragment 6d completes the payload stream.

events.label: recv_frame length 6
events.detail: The server receives exactly the four-byte prefix, decodes length 6, then uses recv_exact for stream.

events.label: Echo validated frame
events.detail: serve_one sends a new length-prefixed frame only after the complete payload has arrived.

events.label: Receive OK echo
events.detail: The client recv_frame succeeds and returns the echoed payload stream.

events.label: EOF and timeout stay distinct
events.detail: A clean close before any byte is EOF and after partial progress is TRUNCATED; a 20 ms empty wait must finish well under 500 ms.

payload.exercise: Complete exercise.c with shared absolute-deadline helpers, partial-I/O loops, framed send/receive, and one-connection echo service behavior.
payload.reference: Use solution.c to compare behavior only after implementing the lesson.h contract.
checks: Back-to-back and fragmented frames over local streams
Oversized declarations that leave payload bytes unread
Clean EOF, truncation, and bounded timeout
Ephemeral 127.0.0.1 service behavior, descriptor cleanup, and listener flag restoration

allowed: Bounded monotonic deadlines on Linux and macOS
excluded: External networking, DNS, raw sockets, or packet capture
Privileged or fixed ports, INADDR_ANY, subprocesses, or shell commands
A general-purpose or internet-facing echo daemon
